newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Maine holders to offer up to NZ$40 mln support.
newsitem.headline: Maine holders to offer up to NZ$40 mln support.

text.p: The principal shareholder in Skellerup New Zealand Ltd, Maine Investments Ltd, said on Friday it was actively developing a "structuring of aspects of its operations" in the face of considerable speculation about the company.

Maine's shareholders would contribute up to NZ$40 million in additional equity and financial support to the company, provided associated rearrangements could be agreed with the banking syndicate, the company said in a statement.
It was optimistic that agreement would be reached soon.

On May 16 Skellerup Finance Ltd said in response to an inquiry by the New Zealand Stock Exchange concerning the fall in price of the company's listed bonds that it was unable to provide an explanation.
The bonds were initially issued in March 1996 with a yield of 10 percent.
The exchange's inquiry was the third in a month attempting to discover why the yield in the bonds had risen so high.

After the Stock Exchange's second request it was revealed that bankers from Boston-based Maine had reduced interest cover ratios for 1997 and brought forward some senior debt pre-payment requirements.

Murray Bolton, who led the leveraged buy-out of the Skellerup Group, told the National Business Review on April 25 that Maine reduced senior debt to $235 million from $315 million. He said then that investor concerns were "unjustified".
The Independent business weekly reported on May 2 on the sudden departure of Skellerup Finance's chief financial officer Wayne McCarthy.
The Skellerup bonds traded as high as 35.05 percent on Friday, but eased back to 30.0 percent.
